sections.herbal_remedies:
About Dermatitis 
 Dermatitis is a common skin condition marked by inflammation, which typically presents as an itchy rash on swollen, red skin. In more severe cases, blistering, oozing, or crusting may occur. It is not a single disease but rather a broad term that encompasses various types and causes of skin irritation. 
 While dermatitis is neither contagious nor life-threatening, it can lead to significant discomfort and emotional distress, often making individuals feel self-conscious about their appearance. 
 Dermatitis can be Acute or Chronic or may be both.
sections.some_types_of_dermatitis:
Atopic dermatitis: causes the skin to itch, scale, swell, and sometimes blister is predominantly there in children; inherited in Families and is often associated with allergies, asthma and stress. 
 Contact dermatitis: The skin develops a pink or red rash, which usually itches. Causes may be irritant or allergic conditions commonly it includes chemical irritants like detergents, soaps, some synthetic fibers, nail polish remover, anti-perspirants, and formaldehyde and some plants like chrysanthemums, daffodils and tulips. 
 Nummular dermatitis: It represents coin-shaped red plaques, most commonly seen on the legs, hands, arms, and torso. More frequent in men than women and the peak age of onset is between 55 and 65. Living in a dry environment or very hot showers results in such conditions. 
 Seborrhoeic dermatitis: This type consists of greasy, yellowish, or reddish scaling on the scalp and other hairy areas, as well as on the face or genitals, and in skin creases along the nose, under the breasts, and elsewhere. It may be aggravated by stress or due to irritation from toxic substances produced by malassezia yeasts
sections.causes_of_dermatitis:
Actual Cause is not known but a combination of Environmental and hereditary factors can be the reason. 

 Allergic or sensitive skin 
 Exposure to an irritant. 

 General predisposing factors 

 Age and familial predisposition. 
 Allergy dust mites, pets, pollens, mold, and dandruff.

Climate and physiological factors like heat, cold, moisture. 
 Food items like dairy products, eggs, nuts and seeds, soy products, wheat. 
 Various other causes are chemicals, plant material, cosmetics, clothing, infectious organisms and certain Drugs. 
 During pregnancy or in the menstrual cycle hormonal changes can worsen the symptoms of Dermatitis.
sections.common_symptoms_of_dermatitis_are:
Redness on skin. 
 Inflammation of skin. 
 Itching in the skin. 
 Dry and flaky skin. 
 Rough and thickened skin. 
 Itchy blisters appears 
 Lichenification – a leathery, thicker skin area appearing in response to scratching. 
 Tiny fluid filled blisters may be seen under the skin “vesicle. 
 When the blisters burst, either by themselves or because of scratching, the fluid oozes onto the surface of the skin. 
 Crusts or scabs formed when the fluid dries. 

 Depending on the type: 



 Intense itching specifies atopic dermatitis. 
 Greyish, yellow scales in and around the ears, on the scalp, or near the eyebrows signal seborrheic dermatitis. In infants, this is called Cradle cap. 
 A red rash limited to a certain area indicates exposure to an irritant. This may be contact dermatitis. 
 Red, itchy, circular patches of crushed skin signifies nummular dermatitis. It is predominant in old people with dry skin, or people living in dry areas. 




 In newborns, a thick and yellowish scalp rash is rarely supplemented by diaper rash. 

 Ayurvedic View for the Cause of Dermatitis 
 According to Ayurveda, Dermatitis results due to incorrect diet and lifestyle, which disturbs the digestion and aggravates Pitta Dosha (Fire). Pitta manifests in the skin and causes the heating, toxins known as Ama get accumulated and then these toxins accumulate in body tissues, infecting them at a deep level and causing Dermatitis.
